text:
morgan: quick heads-up — noticed a big drop in prefix cache hits after last night's compiler prune + kernel selector rollout.

alex: saw that too, metrics look noisy but real. what numbers are you seeing?

morgan: baseline (before rollout) priming-prefix hit ~94% on chat-short workload. post-rollout it's ~38%. p50 gen latency for small requests rose from ~42ms -> ~78ms. token unit cost up ~1.7x on that workload.

riley: ouch. that's huge. any signs it's a keying change (salt/flags) vs cache eviction warmup?

morgan: traced some traces — many requests are generating keys that differ only by a single flag bit introduced by the new kernel metadata. e.g. earlier we used normalized key without kernel bit, now compile step is injecting `kernel_variant` into the key generation path for some models. quick snippet from profiler: 

ci-bot: deploy 4291123000 completed: compiler-prune=true, kernel-selector=v2.1, quant-profile=aggressive

alex: can you paste an example key pair?

morgan: here are two cache keys from consecutive requests for same prompt (sanitized):
```
key_prev = sha1("gpt-big:prompt_hash:ver:v12")
key_new  = sha1("gpt-big:prompt_hash:ver:v12:kernel=v2.1")
```
Both map to same logical context but they're treated as distinct entries. The kernel field is coming from compile-time metadata that used to be ignored.

riley: so it's salting the key unexpectedly. any reason kernel bit was added to key? I thought we intentionally left runtime kernel flags out to maximize reuse.

morgan: me too. looking at the compile diff — `cache_key_salt` now includes `kernel_variant` to avoid cross-kernel cache poisoning. but the implementation accidentally set the salt for "priming cache" namespace (prefix cache) instead of just the model-weight cache.

jamie: this explains why the warmup plateau is failing — all primed contexts are fragmented across kernel variants. hit rate collapse is consistent with that.

alex: temporary mitigation: we can flip the feature-flag to revert salt change for prefix cache only. do we have a quick flag?

morgan: yes — `prefix_cache.include_kernel_salt` is a server config; default was unset and the new compile set it true via the config template. patch ready to set it back to false.

riley: before rolling, can we quantify fragmentation? how many distinct keys per logical prompt now vs before?

morgan: ran a query on the cache index: median distinct-key-per-prompt went from 1 -> 3.2; 95th percentile is ~7. that's enough to kill effective hit rate.

alex: ok. action plan: 1) flip `prefix_cache.include_kernel_salt=false` on canary hosts (eng-runtime-canary-3) 2) run synthetic chat-short replay for 30m 3) if hit rate recovers, roll to prod and open a fix PR to move kernel salt to model-weight namespace only.

jamie: I'll own the canary flip. doing it now.

ci-bot: canary update request submitted (hosts: eng-runtime-canary-3).

morgan: thx. also we should add a unit test that ensures salt fields are namespace-scoped (model vs prefix). this would have caught the template change.

riley: agree. and add a metric that exposes avg distinct-key-per-prompt so we can alert earlier.

alex: logging note: when you revert, capture a before/after sample of key hashes and attach to the incident. helps postmortem.

morgan: will do. preliminary numbers from canary (10m in) — prefix hit climbed from 39% -> 91% on canary. p50 latency back to ~44ms. staging flip looks good.

jamie: i'm scaling canary to 5 hosts and will start gradual rollout. putting a hold on full prod until postmortem & test coverage. :thumbsup:

morgan: thanks. postmortem will include timeline, config template diff, and a proposed test matrix (kernel metadata branches x cache namespaces).

riley: nice catch. small ask — can we add a one-off report that correlates `kernel_selector` values with prefix hit for last 72h? would be nice to verify no other salting bits sneaked in.

alex: filed infra ticket to run the report (INFRA-1421).

ci-bot: note: rolling back config to `prefix_cache.include_kernel_salt=false` on prod scheduled after canary verification.

morgan: closing the loop — keep this thread updated with any anomalies during rollout.
